title: PINN Design–Performance Dependency Matrix
description: A complete qualitative matrix showing how fourteen design dimensions influence seven complementary performance outcomes.
represents: No design element controls a single outcome. The matrix exposes recurring methodological dependencies between representation, physics and numerics, training, structural extension, and the numerical, physical, optimization, cost, robustness, inverse, and reuse properties of a PINN.
interpretation: Influence levels summarize recurring dependencies in the reviewed evidence. They are not effect sizes and do not imply universal monotonic effects. Strength varies with the problem, formulation, and implementation. Trade-off markers identify choices for which improvement in one dimension may increase cost or reduce another.

legend.label: Direct / major dependency
legend.description: A primary design-to-outcome dependency recurring across the synthesis.

legend.label: Context-dependent dependency
legend.description: Influence is substantial but depends strongly on the problem or formulation.

legend.label: Indirect / secondary dependency
legend.description: Influence is mediated through another design element or outcome.

rows.title: Inputs & outputs
rows.detail: Variables, parameters, and the representation interface

evidence.rationale: Coordinate, state, observation, and unknown-parameter interfaces differ between forward and inverse PINN tasks, affecting coverage and identifiability.
Explicit latent parameter inputs enable one model to cover a parameterized PDE family, linking interface design to reuse and parameter efficiency.

rows.title: Architecture / basis
rows.detail: MLP, CNN, GNN, Transformer, KAN, Fourier, RBF, and related bases

evidence.rationale: Fourier-feature architecture changes approximation bias, multi-scale accuracy, and the spectral properties seen by optimization.
A SIREN architecture improves high-frequency field representation while interacting with adaptive sampling and computational efficiency.

rows.title: Activation / features
rows.detail: Tanh, sine, adaptive, Fourier features, and related basis choices

evidence.rationale: Adaptive activations with slope recovery affect solution accuracy and gradient dynamics simultaneously.
Fourier features alter both representable frequency content and the eigenspectrum governing learning.

rows.title: Scaling / non-dimensionalization
rows.detail: Normalization of variables, domains, residuals, and objective components

evidence.rationale: The mixed-variable flow study reports PDE normalization as crucial, supporting scaling as a conditioning and accuracy decision.
Residual stiffness and unequal gradient magnitudes link numerical scaling to conditioning, stability, and final accuracy.

rows.title: Physics-enforcement mechanism
rows.detail: Soft, hard, strong, weak, variational, conservative, and related enforcement forms

evidence.rationale: Exact versus penalty boundary enforcement changes admissibility, approximation error, and loss competition.
Variational enforcement adds test-function and quadrature costs while changing convergence behavior.
Conservative enforcement improves conservation and interface fidelity but introduces a decomposed discrete formulation.

rows.title: Physics / constraints
rows.detail: PDE, IC, BC, interface, conservation, constitutive, and admissibility constraints

evidence.rationale: Equality-constrained training links physical satisfaction to solution accuracy and inverse recovery without treating every requirement as a fixed penalty.
Discrete conservation and interface flux constraints affect physical fidelity, local accuracy, and decomposition cost together.

rows.title: Differentiation / operator evaluation
rows.detail: AD, finite differences, mixed differentiation, spectral methods, and first-order reformulation

evidence.rationale: Coupling automatic and numerical differentiation changes derivative accuracy, residual quality, sparse-point robustness, and computational efficiency.
High-order trace estimation directly trades differentiation formulation against memory and runtime while preserving residual accuracy.

rows.title: Sampling / collocation
rows.detail: Uniform, LHS, Sobol, adaptive, interface-aware, causal, and geometry-aware sampling

evidence.rationale: Across more than 6000 runs, collocation distribution changes accuracy and point efficiency for forward and inverse problems.
Importance sampling improves convergence by reallocating collocation points according to loss information.

rows.title: Loss formulation
rows.detail: Residual, data, BC / IC, conservative, probabilistic, and multi-objective components

evidence.rationale: Composite data, boundary, initial, and PDE losses connect objective construction to accuracy, physics alignment, robustness, and cost.
A Bayesian loss and posterior estimator change inverse consistency, noise robustness, uncertainty, and computational cost.

rows.title: Loss weighting / balancing
rows.detail: Fixed, adaptive, gradient, NTK, augmented-Lagrangian, and related balancing

evidence.rationale: Adaptive loss weights improve error balance and robustness to initial weighting across multiple PDEs.
Gradient-statistic annealing connects weighting to gradient balance, convergence, and predictive accuracy.
Multi-objective gradient conflict affects stability and accuracy and motivates a constrained update direction.

rows.title: Optimizer & LR strategy
rows.detail: Adam, L-BFGS, hybrid, Newton, schedules, and related optimization choices

evidence.rationale: Optimizer choice and differential-operator ill-conditioning jointly determine convergence speed, cost, and final accuracy.
The optimization-process study directly evaluates how optimizer behavior controls PINN competitiveness and achievable accuracy.
Genetic initialization and L-BFGS are combined to improve stability, iteration efficiency, and accuracy.

rows.title: Initialization / training strategy
rows.detail: Pretraining, curriculum, continuation, causal training, and stabilization

evidence.rationale: A staged initialization and fine-optimization workflow changes the basin reached, training time, and solution quality.
Time-piecewise training improves long-domain performance by decomposing temporal optimization into adjustable subnetworks.

rows.title: Decomposition / parallelization
rows.detail: Spatial, temporal, space-time, variable-wise, and other decompositions

evidence.rationale: XPINN couples local specialization, interface transmission, space-time parallelization, and training cost.
Soft trainable decomposition changes generalization, local representation, parameter sharing, and decomposition sensitivity.
Distributed decomposition demonstrates strong scaling and reuse while retaining accuracy on domains far larger than the training domain.

rows.title: Reuse / generalize
rows.detail: Pretrained, enriched, amortized PINN, transfer / meta-learning, operator learning, and reduced order

evidence.rationale: Physics-informed DeepONets amortize a learned solution operator across parametric PDE queries with low online cost.
GPT-PINN reuses pretrained PINNs in a meta-network to reduce repeated training and parameter count.
P2INNs explicitly target repetitive parameterized-PDE training through a latent parameter representation.
Separable PI-DeepONet improves high-dimensional scalability and cuts training time while maintaining accuracy.
